text:
elaine: Quick sync — AcmeBio handoff tomorrow 2pm PT. Need final egress CIDRs + fallback plan if their on‑prem can't reach S3 or our image registry. Who's owning egress rules?

mohit: Infra owns our side, but Acme's net team owns their firewall. @sam is the SG/NAT owner on the private deploy side. We need to allow: 10.1.0.0/16 (customer internal), 52.25.0.0/16 (our hosted egress), and outbound to S3 endpoints on 443.

sam: OK — I'll add SG rules and NAT routes. Will put up a terraform diff in a sec. PR will be small.

sam: Terraform snippet I'm planning to push:
```hcl
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "egress_to_hosted" {
  type        = "egress"
  from_port   = 443
  to_port     = 443
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["52.25.0.0/16", "10.1.0.0/16"]
  description = "Allow outbound to Redwood hosted & customer internal"
}
```

carol: Solutions asked for the exact S3 domain they should allow: s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com — call that out in the runbook. Also request tags on the SG for owner=eng-platform.

mohit: If Acme is fully air‑gapped (no direct egress to S3), they can use our proxy image-sync path. infra-bot shows a private proxy in datacenter-3 (proxy-host-03). We need to confirm TLS and route.

elaine: If the proxy is used, who configures customer side? Is that steps in the private-deploy runbook? Also we need egress monitoring hooks (agent telemetry) for the cutover.

peter: I'll own the proxy/NAT setup for the cutover window. Checklist I'm taking: NAT gateway configured, SG rules applied, route to proxy-host-03, certs deployed, and monitoring alerts wired up. Ping me when PR merged.

sam: PR 4823 opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/4823 — adds SG egress and NAT route. @carol can you review the tags + owner metadata?

carol: Reviewing now. Left two comments re: terraform tags and variable naming. Nothing blocking.

mohit: One airgap blocker flagged by Acme: their internal registry disallows ports 5000-5002, so our image-sync job fails. Options: ask them to open ports, use our offline bundle, or we push images via a jump host. Which path do we prefer? :thinking_face:

elaine: Ben from solutions-engineering will coordinate offline bundle if needed. Ben — can you confirm size and transfer method?

ben: I can. Typical compressed model bundle ~2.1GB per model. We can provide an rsync package or a USB transfer depending on their policy. Need transfer window and contact on their side.

elaine: Acme confirmed transfer window 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-21. Ben will coordinate the rsync option first.

infra-bot: deploy-ops scheduled: private-deploy-acmebio on 1769998900 by sam — status: scheduled.

peter: Also need a fallback: if egress remains blocked at cutover, route live inference traffic to Redwood-hosted with a canary policy. Do we have a service account and cost bucket set?

mohit: Confirmed: service account `redwood-cutover-canary` exists and IAM roles are set. Costs will be charged to trial-customer-acme bucket; finance notified. Documented in runbook under "fallback-to-hosted".

elaine: Action items recap:
- sam: apply SG changes (PR 4823) and post terraform plan output
- peter: proxy + NAT + monitoring and run the proxy steps during cutover
- ben: prepare offline bundle and schedule rsync during transfer window if needed
- carol: finish terraform tag/metadata review
- mohit: verify canary service account docs & confirm cost assignment
- elaine: coordinate cutover timeline and runbook steps, run the 2pm cutover

sam: I'll merge PR after carol approves, then post plan output here.

carol: Approved. Merging now. :white_check_mark:

sam: Plan applied, NAT & SG changes in place. Verified egress to s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com from staging.

peter: Proxy configured and cert deployed. Monitoring dashboards linked in runbook.

elaine: Thanks all — I'll post final pre-flight checklist 1hr before the 2pm cutover. If anyone hits a blocker DM me. :rocket:
